stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The filing cabinet near the door has lost one of their handles.
hints: A pronoun takes the place of a noun. Find the noun that "their" is supposed to point back to.
The handles belong to the filing cabinet. Is the cabinet one thing or many?
A pronoun must match the noun it points back to: one thing takes "its", more than one takes "their". Check the pronoun, then check the other parts.

solution.methodName: Find what the pronoun replaces, then match it

steps.action: Find the noun it points back to: "The filing cabinet". This noun is called the antecedent.
steps.why: The antecedent is the word a pronoun points back to. The handles belong to the cabinet, so the cabinet is the antecedent.

steps.action: "Filing cabinet" is one thing, so it needs a singular pronoun: "its".
steps.why: "Their" is for more than one. "Its" is for one thing or animal.

steps.action: Check the other parts. "near the door" and "has lost" are correct.
The error is "one of their handles". It should be "one of its handles".

trapNotes.near the door: This phrase just tells where the cabinet is. It is correct.
trapNotes.has lost: "Has" matches the singular subject "cabinet", so this part is correct. You may see "handles" and want "have", but "handles" is not the subject.
trapNotes.No error: "Their" sounds natural because "handles" is plural. But the handles belong to one cabinet, so the owner word must be "its".
